parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: $A(a, 0), B(0, b), M\left(\dfrac{a}{2}, \dfrac{b}{2}\right)$; $2a + b = 20$ and $a^2 + b^2 = 100$
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Identifies axis intercepts $A(a, 0)$ and $B(0, b)$, and states midpoint $M\left(\dfrac{a}{2}, \dfrac{b}{2}\right)$. — B1
Substitutes $M\left(\dfrac{a}{2}, \dfrac{b}{2}\right)$ into $2x + y = 10$ to obtain $2a + b = 20$. — M1
Applies distance formula $AB^2 = a^2 + b^2 = 10^2 = 100$. — A1

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Substitutes $b = 20 - 2a$ into $a^2 + b^2 = 100$ to form $5a^2 - 80a + 300 = 0 \implies a^2 - 16a + 60 = 0$. — M1
Solves $(a - 6)(a - 10) = 0$ to select $a = 6$ (since $b = 8 > 0$, rejecting $a = 10$ which gives $b = 0$). — A1
Forms perpendicular bisector through $M(3, 4)$ with gradient $m_{\text{perp}} = \dfrac{3}{4}$ to obtain $3x - 4y + 7 = 0$. — A1
